objectives: Use Simple Past to talk about finished past events (regular -ed verbs + was/were, went, had, did)
Name 8 feeling words and use them in Simple Past sentences
Write and say at least 2 sentences about yesterday

stages.name: Opening — retrieval and bridge
stages.purpose: Activate present-tense daily routine knowledge as the foundation for today's Simple Past input.

procedure.text: Quick fire (oral, whole class): Ask 3 questions using present tense — 'What does Tom do every morning?', 'Which time expression fits: ___ the morning / ___ night / ___ every day?' Students answer chorally or show of hands.
Think-write: 'Write 3 sentences about your daily routine. Use: I get up / eat / go / watch / play.' Prompts on board.
Partner swap — read each other's sentences aloud. One pair shares with the class.

Bridge: 'You just used the present tense — for what you do every day. Today we go back in time. We talk about YESTERDAY — what you did, where you went, how you felt. This is the Simple Past.' Write 'YESTERDAY' on the board. Display the I can... statement: 'I can write 3 sentences about what I did yesterday and how I felt.'

stages.name: Vocabulary — Express Feelings
stages.purpose: Pre-teach 8 feeling words so pupils can use them immediately in Simple Past sentences during the grammar stage.

procedure.text: Show each word with a facial expression or gesture. Say the word, pupils repeat. Cover: happy, sad, tired, excited, bored, scared, angry, surprised. Use the glossary on screen — pupils can click the read-aloud button to hear each word.
Quick check: teacher says the German word, pupils call out the English. 8 words, fast pace.
Model sentence linking vocab to past: 'Yesterday I was tired because I got up at 6.' Pupils repeat.

stages.name: Grammar input — Simple Past
stages.purpose: Introduce the Simple Past rule with explicit German contrast so pupils understand the form before practising it.

procedure.text: Display the grammar explanation. Read the rule aloud: add -ed for regular verbs; irregular set = go/went, be/was/were, have/had, do/did. Walk through each before/after example on screen.

German contrast — say explicitly: 'In German you say Ich habe gespielt. In English: I played — no haben needed.' Write both on board side by side. Then show negation: 'I didn't go to school' (not 'I haven't gone').
Mini board check: teacher says a present-tense sentence, pupils write the Simple Past version on mini whiteboards or paper. 3 items: 'I play / She watches / He goes.' Reveal answers.

stages.name: Guided practice
stages.purpose: Move from supported recognition to guided recall of Simple Past forms, progressing through two difficulty bands.

procedure.text: Hand out (or display) Exercise 1. Read the first item together as a model — show how to use the word bank and the base-form hint in brackets.
Exercise 1 (Band 1 — gap-fill with word bank): complete 5 sentences about yesterday using feelings vocab and Simple Past. Word bank and German instruction provided.
Correct Exercise 1 together — teacher reads each answer, pupils self-mark. Address the 'bored vs boring' distinction from item 5.
Exercise 2 (Band 2 — gap-fill without word bank): 4 sentences, choose the correct Simple Past form from memory. Irregular verb list stays on board as support.
Quick pair check — pupils compare answers. Teacher reveals on board.

stages.name: Production and wrap-up
stages.purpose: Give pupils first independent production of Simple Past + feelings in a low-stakes speaking and writing task.

procedure.text: Display sentence frames. Explain the task: 'Write 2 sentences about yesterday using the frames. Use the Simple Past and at least one feeling word.'
Pupils write 2 sentences individually. A1 frames: 'Yesterday I ___ and I was ___.' / 'In the morning I ___. In the afternoon I ___.' A2 extension: 'Yesterday I was ___ because I ___.'
3-4 pupils share orally. Teacher writes one pupil sentence on board, class checks: correct past form? Correct feeling word? Then revisit the I can... statement — thumbs up if achieved.

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: keep full word bank visible during Exercise 2; allow German translation of feeling words during production; accept A1 sentence frame only. Stronger pupils: Exercise 2 without board support (cover irregular verb list); A2 extension frame; add a third sentence using 'because'. All pupils: mini whiteboard check in grammar stage gives instant low-stakes feedback before written practice.
exercisePlan: Exercise 1 — gap-fill with word bank (Band 1): 5 sentences, Simple Past regular + irregular verbs + feelings vocab, German instruction footnote, first item modelled
Exercise 2 — gap-fill without word bank (Band 2): 4 sentences, regular and irregular Simple Past including negation and question form
Exercise 3 — error correction (Band 3): 4 sentences with German-transfer errors (Perfekt instead of Simple Past, wrong tense, bored/boring confusion, negation error)
